findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_friction.py `resolve_positional_id` reads `lines[number - 1]` of the current log. The test `test_positional_references_resolve_to_content_id` only covers an unshifted log. The spec scenario 'Legacy event identity is stable' says 'after ... an earlier line was removed'.
findings.summary: The spec scenario says a positional `legacy-N` attribution resolves to the stable identity after an earlier line is removed. The implementation resolves N against the current file, so it only works while the log has not shifted. After a removal, `legacy-N` can silently map to a different id-less line, or fail with a named error.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_friction.py:1105 `except RuntimeError as exc:`. `read_operator_config` in `_platform_common.py` calls `read_platform_config`, and the candidate removed the `(FileNotFoundError, OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError)` catch from `platform_repository`. The tests only exercise a `RuntimeError`.
findings.summary: Spec and design say that when the operator configuration cannot be read, the event stays local and pending with a named reason. `route_event` only converts `RuntimeError` into a pending route. `destination_for` and `platform_repository` no longer catch `ValueError`/`OSError`, so a TOML parse or read error from `read_platform_config` or `read_operator_config` is not caught. That error propagates out of `route_event` and `route_pending` instead of becoming a pending route. The same applies to `process_label()` errors inside `route_event`.
